content: Evidence indicates that the patients had stable coronary artery disease without clinical signs of heart failure. The presence of coronary artery disease was confirmed through one or more of the following criteria: a history of myocardial infarction occurring more than three months prior to the screening, coronary revascularization performed more than six months before the screening, angiographic evidence of significant stenosis (defined as at least 70% narrowing of one or more major coronary arteries), or a positive stress test in men with a documented history of chest pain. During a four-week run-in period, all patients were administered perindopril at doses ranging from 2 mg to 8 mg daily. Following this period, the patients were randomly assigned to receive either 8 mg of perindopril once daily (n = 6,110) or a matching placebo (n = 6,108) for a duration of two years. The primary objective of the study was to evaluate the long-term effects of perindopril on the time to the first occurrence of cardiovascular mortality, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or cardiac arrest in patients with stable coronary artery disease. The mean age of the study participants was 60 years. Of the cohort, 85% were male, 92% were on antiplatelet therapy, 63% were taking β-blockers, and 56% were receiving lipid-lowering therapy. The EUROPA study demonstrated that perindopril significantly reduced the relative risk of primary endpoint events. This beneficial effect was primarily attributed to a reduction in the risk of nonfatal myocardial infarction. The positive impact of perindopril on the primary outcome became evident after approximately one year of treatment. The observed outcomes were consistent across all predefined subgroups, regardless of age, underlying disease, or concomitant medication use. Patients should be advised to keep this medication out of the reach of children. For further information, individuals are encouraged to contact the medical communications department toll-free at 1-800-718-9884. Additionally, patients should be informed to report symptoms such as sore throat or fever, as these may indicate neutropenia. The references cited include studies on the effects of perindopril and its combinations on macrovascular and microvascular outcomes in type 2 diabetes mellitus (ADVANCE trial), the impact of perindopril-based blood pressure-lowering regimens on recurrent stroke risk (PROGRESS trial), and the role of perindopril in preventing mortality in Duchenne muscular dystrophy over a 10-year follow-up period. Other studies explored the electrophysiological changes associated with angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibition post-myocardial infarction and the comparative efficacy of amiodarone alone versus amiodarone combined with losartan or perindopril in preventing atrial fibrillation recurrence in patients with lone paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
